chunks: From him, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who bought an animal but did not have its price with him, so he went to one of his companions and said, 'So-and-so, pay for me, and the profit is between me and you.' So he paid for him, and the animal died. He (the Imam) said, 'The price is upon both of them, because if it were profit, it would be between them both.'

key_terms.الثَّمَنُ عَلَيْهِمَا: The price is upon both of them
key_terms.دَابَّة: Animal (specifically a beast of burden or livestock)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on financial loss when a partner buys an animal with shared funds and it dies?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the ruling of *Qard* (interest-free loan) within a profit-sharing context, establishing that if the asset perishes, the lender bears the financial loss while the borrower retains the liability for the principal, as profit sharing does not equate to joint ownership of capital. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) uses the logic that since profit was shared, the risk of capital loss remains with the provider, a foundational principle in Shia commercial jurisprudence distinguishing between loan and partnership. This ruling ensures fairness by preventing the lender from losing both capital and profit share when the asset is lost through no fault of the borrower.
